recommendation.justification: Satellite NDWI (-0.35) and lack of recent rainfall indicate critical moisture deficit that threatens boll development and yield. Soil health is excellent (score 92, optimal pH, balanced nutrients) and canopy vigor is high (NDVI 0.75), so restoring water will allow the crop to realize its yield potential and capture strong market prices (7,618 INR/quintal). Immediate irrigation also reduces the risk of drought‑induced Fusarium and Verticillium wilts.
actions: Verify availability of flood‑irrigation water and ensure pumps/channels are operational.
Apply flood irrigation to deliver approximately 30 mm of water per event, repeating every 7–10 days until NDWI rises above 0.10.
After each irrigation, measure soil moisture at 30 cm depth (tensiometer or portable sensor) to confirm field capacity is reached.
Apply a thin layer of organic mulch (straw or shredded leaves) on the soil surface to curb evaporation and protect against erosion.
Conduct weekly scouting for Fusarium and Verticillium wilt symptoms; if observed, initiate recommended fungicide program.
